title: [P1] bunker-las-03 port range pool exhausted — spawn failure path leaks port allocations
detail: Cell: [run_battery] FAIL — spawn failed on bunker-las-03: "spawn attempt 2 failed: bunker: spawn agent: internal: port range allocation: no free port ranges available (pool exhausted: 10 ranges)". Root cause verified in bunker v0.1.0 source (~/go/pkg/mod/github.com/deploy!bunker/bunker@v0.1.0/internal/agent/manager.go): Spawn() calls portAlloc.Allocate(agentID) at step 1.5 (line 133) BEFORE the capacity check (line 145, which returns 'capacity full' WITHOUT freeing) and the cleanup() closure (lines 156-178) only rolls back user/keys — it NEVER calls m.portAlloc.Free(agentID). Any spawn that fails after allocation (useradd, dockerd, container step) leaks one range for the life of the bunkerd process; the allocator is in-memory (allocated map + free stack, never persisted/rebuilt from live agents), so leaked ranges only return on daemon restart, while orphans persist. Evidence: server ONLINE, uptime 15h49m, but only 1/8 agents tracked (219ef0c3, port range 30700-30799) while all 10 pool ranges are marked allocated — 9 ranges leaked. Every subsequent spawn attempt fails at allocation, permanently blocking the terminal-jail battery until bunkerd restarts.

title: [P1] Shipped YAML rules mirror is loaded as USER rules and weakens 12 engine verdicts — pattern parity is not CI-enforced
detail: install.sh copies plugin/terminal_jail/rules/00-builtins.yaml to ~/.config/terminal-jail/rules.d/, which the engine's Decider loads as USER rules; _build_layers applies SAME-ID OVERRIDE, so on any host that ran the documented install path the YAML patterns REPLACE the hardcoded builtins. The YAML patterns are weaker than the Python builtins (auto-script, builtin-fork-bomb whitespace tolerance, builtin-mkfs quoted argv) and flip 12 verdicts from block/modify to allow. Evidence (foreman tick #263): bare .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q on kara-lair = 12 failed / 295 passed / 13 skipped, identical failure set at pristine HEAD 70befdb; with TERMINAL_JAIL_INTERRUPTOR_USER_RULES_DIR=/nonexistent the suite is 307 passed / 13 skipped / 0 failed. Same finding filed 2026-09-03 by the QA battery (skill ref yaml-mirror-user-rules-override-2026-09-03.md) but never taskified. CI stays green because it runs in a fresh container with no user rules dir and the mirror test asserts ids/counts only, never patterns.
reasoning: Fix shape: (a) make the shipped YAML express the argv-quoting/interpreter-script semantics of the hardcoded builtins, OR make the engine prefer hardcoded built-ins over same-id file rules; (b) upgrade plugin/test_packaging.py::test_shipped_rules_yaml_mirrors_engine_builtin_ids to compare PATTERNS (or assert RuleLoader behaviour parity) instead of ids/counts; (c) extend scripts/yaml-mirror-parity-probe.py to pattern equality across all rules; (d) fix the YAML header comment count (says 29 rules/11 blocklist while 12 blocklist ids exist). Discovered by the CLN-1 worker (commit 13a14a4) and reproduced by the CLN-1 tier-2 judge.
